headline_marked: Executive Magistrate appointed to [[exhume Salman Shah's remains]] for cause of death
headline: Executive Magistrate appointed to exhume Salman Shah's remains for cause of death
summary: A court order has paved the way for the exhumation of the legendary actor's remains to determine the actual cause of his death in 1996.
details: An executive magistrate has been appointed to oversee the process of exhuming the remains of actor Salman Shah to determine the actual cause of his death.
The appointment was made through an office order issued by the Additional District Magistrate of Sylhet, Pinki Saha, on June 22.

According to court sources, the process follows a directive from the Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Court on May 24, which ordered the exhumation, preparation of an inquest report, and a post-mortem examination.
The CID inspector, Ziaul Morshed, had applied for the exhumation of the body as part of an ongoing investigation into the actor's death.
Salman Shah died on September 6, 1996, at a house in Iskaton, Dhaka. While initially reported as an unnatural death, later allegations of murder were filed.
The case has been investigated by multiple agencies over the years, and it is currently under re-investigation by court order.
However, the case's plaintiff, Mohammad Alamgir (Kumkum), has recently applied to the court to cancel the exhumation order.
caption:

headline_marked: 61 passengers [[vanish from Malaysia-bound flight]] at Shahjalal Airport
headline: 61 passengers vanish from Malaysia-bound flight at Shahjalal Airport
summary: A total of 76 passengers attempted to travel to Malaysia on 'body contracts,' but 61 of them disappeared before boarding the aircraft.
details: At Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, 61 passengers disappeared before they could board a flight destined for Malaysia.
The incident involved a group of 76 passengers who were attempting to travel to Malaysia under what is known as 'body contracts.'
Authorities reported that while the process was underway, a significant majority of the group vanished from the terminal.
The disappearance of these passengers has raised concerns regarding the legality and nature of the travel arrangements made via these contracts.
Security and airport officials are now looking into how such a large number of passengers could disappear from the airport premises.
caption:
61 passengers vanished from a Malaysia-bound flight at Shahjalal Airport. What happened to the group traveling on 'body contracts'?

At Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, 61 passengers disappeared before they could board a flight destined for Malaysia.

The incident involved a group of 76 passengers who were attempting to travel to Malaysia under what is known as 'body contracts.'

Authorities reported that while the process was underway, a significant majority of the group vanished from the terminal.

The disappearance of these passengers has raised concerns regarding the legality and nature of the travel arrangements made via these contracts.

Security and airport officials are now looking into how such a large number of passengers could disappear from the airport premises.
